  "text": "Every morning, Arthur opened the station bookstall at six, though the first train no longer stopped until seven.

He liked the hour in between. He swept the platform, boiled his kettle, and turned the newspapers so their headlines faced the tracks.

One Tuesday, he found a crossword tucked beneath the shutter. Only one answer had been filled in.

Seventeen across: a place to begin again.

HOME, someone had written, incorrectly. The answer required five letters.

Arthur pencilled START beside it and left the page on the counter.

The next morning it returned with three more answers and a correction to his own.

Over the following weeks, they completed six crosswords without meeting. His partner knew rivers, composers, and obscure birds. Arthur supplied footballers and things found in sheds.

Then a note appeared in the margin.

Last treatment Thursday. Might be late.

Arthur read it twice. He left the crossword unfinished.

On Thursday he kept the kettle warm until noon.

At eleven forty, a woman in a yellow coat approached the stall. She held a folded newspaper against her chest.

“I think you've got my pencil,” she said.

Arthur looked at the three pencils in his mug.

“Which one?”

“The good one.”

He gave her the chair from behind the counter and made tea in his spare cup.

For a while they worked without speaking. A train arrived, emptied, and went away.

“Nine down,” she said eventually. “Six letters. Someone you've yet to meet.”

“Stranger,” Arthur said.

“That's eight.”

He counted on his fingers, frowned, and passed her the pencil.

“You'd better keep this.”"
